3. **Restart safety — the body's unverified hypothesis, RESOLVED as
   "escalate, do not auto-restart" (v1).** Probed live: the daemon is a
   manually-started orphaned node process
   (`node .../happy/dist/index.mjs daemon start-sync`, pid 201205, started
   2026-08-04 21:30 local — i.e. the manual recovery that ended this very
   outage), and there is **NO systemd unit** (`systemctl [--user] list-units`
   returns nothing for happy). A non-interactive start path DOES exist
   (`happy daemon start`, detached). But a cron-context restart is NOT
   obviously safe: per `.claude/rules/background-automation.md` § tmux
   socket-dir contract item 6, post-restart durability hinges on starting the
   daemon FROM A LOGIN SHELL so `~/.profile` sources `scripts/eps_tmux_env.sh`
   and `TMUX_TMPDIR` resolves to the fleet's single tmux server; the watcher's
   cron env does not source the profile, so a cron-started daemon risks the
   #1466 split-brain class (a second tmux server, sessions invisible to
   `tmux ls`). Second hazard: the probe failing does not prove the daemon
   process is dead (`_daemon_reachable` returns False for a HUNG-but-alive
   daemon too), so an unguarded start would double-daemon. Plan-time
   resolution: v1 is ESCALATE-ONLY (the body's own stated fallback — "if
   unsafe, the arm should escalate loudly … rather than restart"); any restart
   arm, if planned at all, is opt-in, login-shell-invoked, and gated on
   positive proof the recorded daemon pid is gone.
